_source: VERIFIED by reading the file: this cached page is an Angular SPA shell, not a product page. Title is `Siemens SiePortal`, the root element carries `data-beasties-container`, and the catalog number S55499-D820 appears ZERO times in the 31 kB of HTML — the real content is fetched by JavaScript from the SiePortal/pview APIs, which is why siemens.ts goes to those APIs instead of parsing this HTML.
_tier: value-verified NEGATIVE case. Unlike the other extracted -page fixtures (noise-guard tier), this one asserts a specific, checked outcome.

_notes.why: A JS shell must yield NOTHING rather than scraps of application chrome. The generic parser already gets this right — `requireCatalogNumber` makes it bail with 'Fallback page did not contain the catalog number' — and this fixture pins that behaviour so a future widening of the admission gates cannot start mining an empty shell.
_notes.opportunity: The pipeline learns nothing from this shape today. Recognising 'HTML shell + catalog number absent + framework markers present' as its own diagnosis would let discovery escalate straight to the browser or to a known API, instead of recording it as a page that simply failed to parse — see COLD-START-PLAN §2A and §3.2 (per-field causal blockers).
